newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk shipyard should be liquidated - administrator.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk shipyard should be liquidated - administrator.

text.p: The administrator of Poland's bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard said on Monday the company's financial situation was so bad that it should be liquidated, unless a significant injection of capital for it was found.

Michal Lachert told Reuters that offers by two foreign consortia offers to invests in the shipyard inspired little hope to save the company. He added the privatisation ministry had no concrete plans how restructure the company.
"A careful analyses showed the shipyard's own funds are not sufficient to cover debts taken by the administrator. It makes any activity impossible," he said.

Lachert said one investment offer was from a Polish company with a Norwegian capital, ready to invest $200 million, and the other from a Vienna-based company. He did not give any about the second offer.
He added that Polish banks, including Bank Gdanski, state-owned Pekao SA and Bank Handlowy SA, had refused new loans for the shipyard during recent negotiations.
"Even if a bank did (give a loan), the cost of the loan would be so big, that even if price for the ship was good, its building would not pay off," he said.

Meanwhile, about 1,000 shipyard workers staged a rally to protest against actions by the administrator, saying he was taking care only of creditors' interests and neglected the company's restructuring.
"We have to be determined in our fight for our jobs, because the administrator wants only a complete liquidation of the shipyard," said Jerzy Borowczak, Solidarity trade union leader in the yard.
The shipyard, where Lech Walesa's Solidarity union was born 16 years ago, has debts of 414 million zlotys ($151 million) while its assets are worth about 350 million zlotys. It employs 6,000 people.
The shareholders of the Gdansk shipyard, in which the treasury has a majority, decided to file for bankruptcy in June after the yard's debts exceeded its assets and banks denied it loans.
